64	static uint64_t magicmem[8] __attribute__((aligned(64)));
65	
66	/* The host (SimControl) reads magicmem straight from RAM, behind the
67	 * hart's caches, so write back L1 (and L2 if present) before handing the
68	 * command over. CCTL command 6 = L1D_WBINVAL_ALL, 0x12 = L2_WBINVAL_ALL.
69	 * On QEMU the CSR write is accepted and memory is coherent anyway. */
70	static void flush_dcache(void)
71	{
72	  __asm__ __volatile__("csrw mcctlcommand, %0" ::"rK"(6));
73	#if __riscv_xlen == 64
74	  /* L2 writeback, gated to rv64 because it uses rv64-only ld/sd to reach the
75	   * 64-bit L2C MMIO registers (mmsc_cfg bit 46 is the L2-present flag) -- it
76	   * cannot COMPILE on rv32. Whether to flush is still decided at runtime by the
77	   * bit-46 check inside the asm. An rv32 core WITH an L2C would need a
78	   * 32-bit-halves access path here; today's rv32 target (d23) has no L2, so the
79	   * L1 writeback above suffices. */
80	  __asm__ __volatile__(
81	    "csrr    t0, mmsc_cfg\n"

#ifndef MEMORY_MAP_H
#define MEMORY_MAP_H

/* RAM Bridge. Range covers QEMU `virt`-machine RAM base (0x80000000) so
 * the same ELF can be loaded at the same physical address in both halves
 * of the hybrid handoff. The cap stops below NDS_HVM_BASE (0x90000000)
 * to avoid colliding with the CPU's HVM slave port. */
#define RAM_BASE 0x0
#define RAM_END 0x8FFFFFFF

/* Hart0 ILM SLAVEPORT */
#define HART0_ILM_BASE 0xA0000000
#define HART0_ILM_END 0xA01FFFFF

/* Hart0 DLM SLAVEPORT */
#define HART0_DLM_BASE 0xA0200000
#define HART0_DLM_END 0xA03FFFFF

/* Simulation control region */
#define SIM_CONTROL_BASE 0xE0080000
#define SIM_CONTROL_END 0xE0080FFF

/* Debug Module */
#define PLDM_BASE 0xE6800000
#define PLDM_END 0xE6800FFF

/* ACM (Andes Custom Memory) region */
#define ACM0_BASE 0xC0000000
#define ACM0_END 0xC0000FFF

/* AIA Machine-Level Interrupt File */
#define MLIF_BASE 0xC4000000
#define MLIF_END 0xC40FFFFF

/* AIA Supervisor-Level/Guest Interrupt File */
#define SLIF_BASE 0xC4100000
#define SLIF_END 0xC41FFFFF

/* SMU */
#define SMU_BASE 0xF0100000
#define SMU_END 0xF01FFFFF

/* UART1 */
#define UART1_BASE 0xF0200000
#define UART1_END 0xF02FFFFF

/* UART2 */
#define UART2_BASE 0xF0300000
#define UART2_END 0xF03FFFFF

/* AX66 Alias Region to RAM Bridge */
#define RAM_ALIAS_BASE 0x800000000
#define RAM_ALIAS_END 0x87FFFFFFF

#endif /* MEMORY_MAP_H */

No - andesim does not transport MMIO device state today, and there is no automatic way to "copy" QEMU's MMIO writes into vsim. The handoff moves exactly two things: hart architectural state (`hybrid_state_v1`: GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V/PMP/Andes block) and RAM (the /dev/shm shared mmap). Device registers are inside each simulator's own device model, so whatever QEMU wrote stays in QEMU; vsim's devices start at RTL reset.

Whether you must re-set a region in vsim depends on which of 3 cases it falls in:

**1. Devices vsim does not decode at all - most of the AE350 map.**
vsim's platform maps only: RAM, ILM/DLM, ACM, AIA IF, SimControl (0xE0080000), Debug Module, SMU, UART1/UART2 (`vsim_andesim/src/platform/memory_map.h`). PLIC, PLMT, PIT, WDT, RTC, GPIO, DMAC, etc. do not exist in vsim. You cannot transport them, and you don't need to: their config only matters for the QEMU phase. The ROI is trap-free and interrupt-free by contract, so PLIC/PLMT setup is irrelevant inside the window. The only rule: ROI code must never touch these addresses - in vsim they are unmapped and the access would fault.

**2. Devices both engines model and the ROI uses live.**
UART2 (printf) and SimControl/HTIF already work: the ROI's own loads/stores go straight to the vsim model. Their QEMU-phase register config is not copied, but today's vsim models don't depend on it.

**3. Device config that changes ROI timing - the L2C register block (0xE0500000) is the canonical case.**
This is the same problem as `mcache_ctl` (L1 enable), but through MMIO instead of a CSR, so the existing CSR transport does NOT cover it. Right now it is moot:

- The shipped engine has no L2: `Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc` says `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB 0`, so `has_shared_cache = false` and the core reports mmsc_cfg.L2C=0 (the vplat runtime already guards its L2C access on that bit, `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c:86`).
- QEMU's "L2C" at 0xE0500000 is only a writable RAM stub (`memory_region_init_ram`, `qemu_andesim/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1492`) - no function, and it is private QEMU RAM, not part of the shared mmap, so its contents don't survive the handoff either.

For a future engine built WITH an L2C, yes - the enable/config writes from the QEMU phase would have to be replayed into vsim, or the window runs with L2 at reset (off) and the cycle figure inflates, exactly like the mcache_ctl story. The natural mechanism: vsim resumes exactly at the ROI entry, so the program itself has no chance to redo device init; the injection point is `ResumeDriver` - replay a small whitelist of MMIO registers via Program-Buffer store instructions before `dret` (the same machinery the V-scratch sweep uses), with the QEMU side draining those values into the handoff. That is a design extension, not something in the code today.

input.description: Explore andesim drain/ABI/verify
input.prompt:
Explore the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim (read-only; also the ABI submodule at /home/nick/work/andesim/include). Goal: gather what is needed to plan a new "L2C MMIO config transport" feature: QEMU plugin drains L2 cache controller registers (MMIO at 0xE0500000) into the hybrid_state_v1 wire struct, vsim restores them, driver --verify compares them.

Report on:
1. include/hybrid/state_abi.h — full current structure: version constant/field, flags (HYBRID_FLAG_*), how the v3 Andes block was added (struct hybrid_andes_csr + HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST X-macro), size/static-assert/versioning conventions, and what adding a new block (v4) must touch. Note the git submodule status (is include/ a submodule pinned by SHA? check .gitmodules and git -C include log --oneline -3).
2. qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c — how the plugin reads state today: register access API (qemu_plugin_reg_* via gdbstub names?), how the Andes CSR block is drained and how HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is decided, where the drain happens (trigger callback), and critically: what memory-read APIs exist in the vendored qemu_plugin/qemu-plugin.h (search for qemu_plugin_read_memory_vaddr, qemu_plugin_read_memory, hwaddr variants, and the QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION). Can the plugin read guest physical/virtual memory at an arbitrary address (0xE0500000) at drain time? Also check how the plugin currently learns ram_base/ram_size or other config from args.
3. The driver verify path: find state_diff (driver/*.cpp) — how fields are compared, how gated blocks (flags) are handled, how per-field exclusions (mip, msp_bound, milmb) are implemented, and where an L2C block compare would be added. Also how the driver invokes vsim with the handoff file and which args pass v_scratch_gpa or similar per-feature parameters (driver/cmd_run.cpp).
4. The mcache_ctl precedent (L21): find where mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl transport was implemented across plugin + docs + tests — closest analog to L2C-enable-for-cycle-accuracy. Which tests cover it (tests/, tests/andes_sim/, tests/hybrid/e2e_*)?
5. Fixture + e2e patterns: tests/fixtures/Makefile structure, one representative rt_c_* fixture source (how ROI markers are used, how pre-ROI init code looks), tests/e2e.sh flow for hybrid mode (how QEMU1 is launched with the plugin, how vsim is launched, how verify is invoked), and how per-engine tests are registered under tests/engines/ (gen_manifest.py, csr_restore_table.md role).
6. Docs to update: which sections of docs/USER_GUIDE.md and CLAUDE.md describe the CSR restore split / transported state (so the plan can list doc updates).
Return: concrete file paths + line-level facts, short quotes for load-bearing details, and clear answers per question. No file dumps.

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 4 (M-ext): append struct hybrid_m_ext_csr after the Andes block --
25	// the writable M-mode CSRs across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA (NMI, CLIC, perf
26	// counters, trap-save, triggers, state-enable, ...), transported forward-looking
27	// and capability-gated per engine. Version 3 (Andes F0) appended
28	// struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to
29	// 128 bytes/register. Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers
30	// check magic + version + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
31	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 4u
32	
33	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
34	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
35	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
36	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
37	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
38	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
39	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
40	// v4: the struct hybrid_m_ext_csr block carries live values (the producer's
41	// gdbstub advertised at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the block is
42	// all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
43	#define HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT (1u << 4)
44	
45	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
46	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
47	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
48	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
49	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
50	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
51	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
52	
53	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
54	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
55	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
56	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
57	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
58	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
59	
60	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
61	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
62	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
63	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
64	
65	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
66	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
67	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
68	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
69	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
70	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
71	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
72	
73	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
74	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
75	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
76	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
77	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
78	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
79	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
80	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
81	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
82	  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
83	  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
84	  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
85	  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
86	  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
87	  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
88	  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
89	  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
90	  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
91	  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
92	  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
93	  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
94	
95	// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
96	// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
97	// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
98	// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
99	struct hybrid_andes_csr {
100	#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
101	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
102	#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
103	  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
104	  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
105	};
106	
107	// v4: the writable M-mode CSRs across the whole AndeStar V5 SPA that a
108	// bare-metal M / M+U ROI can hold as plain architectural state -- everything
109	// the spec defines as readable+writable with no read/write side effects, minus
110	// the blocks already carried above (standard M trap CSRs, the v3 Andes block,
111	// PMP, PMA, FP, V). Same single-source-of-truth X-macro pattern as
112	// HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST: X(field, csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (plugin
113	// drain, ResumeDriver restore, StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify)
114	// iterates this list, so adding a CSR is one line. Each is capability-gated by
115	// CSR address (src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp): an engine that lacks the feature
116	// no-ops the restore/drain, so the block is transported forward-looking -- a
117	// core that implements it (CLIC, Smrnmi, Smstateen, ePMP, ...) round-trips it
118	// with no further change. Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
119	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)                \
120	  X(menvcfg,         0x30A, "menvcfg")          \
121	  X(mseccfg,         0x747, "mseccfg")          \
122	  X(mcounteren,      0x306, "mcounteren")       \
123	  X(mcountinhibit,   0x320, "mcountinhibit")    \
124	  X(mhpmcounter3,    0xB03, "mhpmcounter3")     \
125	  X(mhpmcounter4,    0xB04, "mhpmcounter4")     \
126	  X(mhpmcounter5,    0xB05, "mhpmcounter5")     \
127	  X(mhpmcounter6,    0xB06, "mhpmcounter6")     \
128	  X(mhpmevent3,      0x323, "mhpmevent3")       \
129	  X(mhpmevent4,      0x324, "mhpmevent4")       \
130	  X(mhpmevent5,      0x325, "mhpmevent5")       \
131	  X(mhpmevent6,      0x326, "mhpmevent6")       \
132	  X(mcounterwen,     0x7CE, "mcounterwen")      \
133	  X(mcounterinten,   0x7CF, "mcounterinten")    \
134	  X(mcountermask_s,  0x7D2, "mcountermask_s")   \
135	  X(mcountermask_u,  0x7D3, "mcountermask_u")   \
136	  X(mnscratch,       0x740, "mnscratch")        \
137	  X(mnepc,           0x741, "mnepc")            \
138	  X(mncause,         0x742, "mncause")          \
139	  X(mnstatus,        0x744, "mnstatus")         \
140	  X(mnvec,           0x7C3, "mnvec")            \
141	  X(mrnxvec,         0x7DE, "mrnxvec")          \
142	  X(mdcause,         0x7C9, "mdcause")          \
143	  X(mslideleg,       0x7D5, "mslideleg")        \
144	  X(msavestatus,     0x7D6, "msavestatus")      \
145	  X(msaveepc1,       0x7D7, "msaveepc1")        \
146	  X(msavecause1,     0x7D8, "msavecause1")      \
147	  X(msaveepc2,       0x7D9, "msaveepc2")        \
148	  X(msavecause2,     0x7DA, "msavecause2")      \

173	#define HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM 51
174

182	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by

186	  uint32_t version;

210	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];

213	  uint64_t vtype;
214	  uint64_t vl;
215	  uint64_t vlenb;

# Plan: Transport L2C enable/config across the QEMU -> vsim handoff

## Context (why)

Today the hybrid handoff moves only **hart architectural state** (`hybrid_state_v1`:
GPR/FPR/CSR/V/PMP/Andes/M-ext) and **RAM** (the `/dev/shm` shared mmap). **MMIO device
registers are not transported** - each simulator keeps its own device model, so config
QEMU wrote stays in QEMU and vsim's devices start at RTL reset.

The **L2 cache controller (L2C)** is an MMIO block at `0xE0500000` (DS220 24.2 Table 259).
Its **Control Register (offset 0x0008)** holds the L2 enable bit (`CEN`) plus prefetch/ECC/
RAM-timing config. This is **boot-static config that changes ROI cycle behavior on an
L2-enabled engine** - exactly the problem `mcache_ctl` (L1 enable) already solves for the
cycle figure (`resume_driver.hpp:323`), but through **MMIO instead of a CSR**, so the
existing CSR transport does NOT cover it.

**Forward-looking:** every current vsim engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` (no L2C
region). So this feature must **no-op cleanly today** and **activate automatically when an
L2-enabled engine is built**. This mirrors how the v4 M-ext block is transported
forward-looking and capability-gated.

## What DS220 11.8.5 / 24.2 establish (extracted from the PDF)

- L2C region: `0xE0500000 - 0xE05FFFFF` (matches QEMU memmap and `config.inc`
  `NDS_L2C_REG_BASE=0x00000000E0500000`).
- **Control Register @ +0x0008 (11.8.7), RW** - the enable/config word:
  `CEN[0]` (L2 enable, **reset = 1**), `PFTHRES[2:1]` prefetch throttle (reset 0),
  `IPFDPT`/`DPFDPT` depth, `ECCEN[7]`, `TRAMOCTL/TRAMICTL/DRAMOCTL/DRAMICTL[13:8]` RAM
  timing, `INITSTATUS[14]` (RO status). **This is the register the feature transports.**
- Configuration Register @ +0x0000 (11.8.6): **RO** (SIZE/ECC/MAP derived by HW) - nothing
  to restore, same as `mpl2cm_cfg` in the manifest ("read-only constant, the engine derives it").
- Way Allocation Mask @ +0x0300.. (11.8.17): RW, only matters if a workload partitions L2.
- CCTL command/status, HPM control/counter, error registers: operational/volatile - not boot config.
- **Access rule (11.8.3): single transfer, size < 8 bytes, device non-bufferable.**
  => transport with **4-byte `sw`/`lw`**, NOT 8-byte `sd`/`ld`. All meaningful control
  bits live in the low 32 bits, so one `sw` to 0x0008 covers the whole enable/config word.

## Design decisions (user was away for the scope question - these are the recommended defaults)

1. **Scope = Control Register (0x0008) only.** This is precisely the "enable/config" asked
   for. Wire struct is one `uint64_t`. Way-mask is left as a documented, append-only
   extension point (append to the struct + one more `sw` per register when a partitioning
   workload needs it). *Revisit if you want way-mask now.*
2. **Fix QEMU's reset default.** QEMU models L2C as a **zero-initialized RAM stub**
   (`hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1492`, `memory_region_init_ram`). DS220 says `CEN` resets to 1.
   A guest that relies on the default and never writes 0x0008 would drain `CEN=0` and
   wrongly disable L2 in vsim. Proper fix (not a workaround): **initialize the L2C control
   word to its reset value (CEN=1) at machine init**, so an untouched register drains
   faithfully.

## Architecture / data flow (the core to understand)

```
  QEMU phase                         handoff file                vsim phase
  ----------                         ------------                ----------
  guest sw -> 0xE0500008  ]                                   [ ResumeDriver (hart halted):
  (L2C RAM stub, reset     ] drain   hybrid_state_v1  restore  ]   PB: sw ctrl -> 0xE0500008
   value CEN=1 seeded)     ]-------> .l2c.ctrl  +      ------->]   ONLY if engine has L2C
  plugin reads it via      ]         HYBRID_FLAG_L2C           ]   (else skipped - a store to
  qemu_plugin_read_             ^                              ]    an absent region faults)
  memory_hwaddr(0xE0500008)     |                             [ StateDrain: PB lw readback
                          drain-time MMIO read                    -> .l2c.ctrl (for --verify)
```

Three properties that make this safe:
- **Hard capability gate on restore.** Unlike tolerant CSR writes (an absent CSR no-ops),
  a PB store to an unmapped `0xE0500008` **faults the Program Buffer** (`exec_progbuf`
  throws). So the store is issued **only when the vsim engine has an L2C**
  (`has_shared_cache = NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`, `ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp:45`).
  On today's engines the restore is skipped entirely - clean no-op.
- **Flag-gated wire block.** `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C` is set by the plugin only when it can read
  the region; clear means the block is zero and every consumer skips it (same discipline as
  `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` / `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`).
- **4-byte accesses** per the DS220 bus rule.

## Feature slices (independent; complete ONE per session, TDD each; update states here)

Each slice is RED (write failing test) -> GREEN (smallest code) -> REFACTOR, per TDD.md.

- **F1 - ABI v5 block.** [ ]
  `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (submodule `andesim_abi`): add `struct hybrid_l2c { uint64_t
  ctrl; }`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C (1u<<5)`, append `struct hybrid_l2c l2c;` after `m_ext`, bump
  `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION` to 5, shrink `reserved[]` to keep total size, update
  `state_abi_check.h` static-asserts (offset + size). RED: the size/offset static-assert or
  `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (external vsim) fails until fields land. Commit as a
  submodule bump pinned by SHA.

- **F2 - PB store/load word encoders.** [ ]
  `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp`: add `encode_sw`/`encode_lw` (funct3=010,
  STORE/LOAD opcodes) beside `encode_sd`/`encode_ld`. RED: unit test asserting the exact
  32-bit encodings against hand-computed values (mirror existing encoder tests).

- **F3 - ResumeDriver L2C restore.** [ ]
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`: after the `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` block
  (`:331`), add `restore_l2c(state)` guarded by `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C` AND the engine-L2C-present
  cap. Sequence reuses existing primitives: `write_register_abstract(bus_, regno_gpr(A),
  l2c_base+0x8)`, `write_register_abstract(bus_, regno_gpr(V), state.l2c.ctrl)`,
  `exec_progbuf({encode_sw(V, A, 0)})`. Use post-GPR-loop scratch regs (x5-x7 are free
  there, per the mcycle comment `:339`). RED: recording_bus unit test asserts the DMI
  write sequence (data0/data1 + access-register command + progbuf words + exec) and that a
  cleared flag / absent cap issues **nothing**.

- **F4 - StateDrain L2C readback.** [ ]
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`: in `drain_with_passthrough`, after the CSR drains
  and before/with the V dump, add `drain_l2c(state)`: `write_register_abstract(addr)`,
  `exec_progbuf({encode_lw(V, A, 0)})`, `read_register_64(regno_gpr(V))` -> `state.l2c.ctrl`.

## What DS220 11.8.5 / 24.2 establish (extracted from the PDF)

- L2C region: `0xE0500000 - 0xE05FFFFF` (matches QEMU memmap and `config.inc`

  `IPFDPT`/`DPFDPT` depth, `ECCEN[7]`, `TRAMOCTL/TRAMICTL/DRAMOCTL/DRAMICTL[13:8]` RAM

  to restore, same as `mpl2cm_cfg` in the manifest ("read-only constant, the engine derives it").
- Way Allocation Mask @ +0x0300.. (11.8.17): RW, only matters if a workload partitions L2.
- CCTL command/status, HPM control/counter, error registers: operational/volatile - not boot config.
- **Access rule (11.8.3): single transfer, size < 8 bytes, device non-bufferable.**
  => transport with **4-byte `sw`/`lw`**, NOT 8-byte `sd`/`ld`. All meaningful control
  bits live in the low 32 bits, so one `sw` to 0x0008 covers the whole enable/config word.

Today the hybrid handoff moves only **hart architectural state** (`hybrid_state_v1`:

The **L2 cache controller (L2C)** is an MMIO block at `0xE0500000` (DS220 24.2 Table 259).
Its **Control Register (offset 0x0008)** holds the L2 enable bit (`CEN`) plus prefetch/ECC/

cycle figure (`resume_driver.hpp:323`), but through **MMIO instead of a CSR**, so the
existing CSR transport does NOT cover it.

**Forward-looking:** every current vsim engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` (no L2C
region). So this feature must **no-op cleanly today** and **activate automatically when an

forward-looking and capability-gated.

- L2C region: `0xE0500000 - 0xE05FFFFF` (matches QEMU memmap and `config.inc`

  to restore, same as `mpl2cm_cfg` in the manifest ("read-only constant, the engine derives it").

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp)

# hotloops: C++ replacement for QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh.
add_executable(hotloops hotloops.cpp elf_syms.cpp process.cpp)
target_include_directories(hotloops PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(hotloops PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
set_target_properties(hotloops PROPERTIES
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
foreach(_t andesim-cli-test andesim-json-test andesim-infra-test andesim-plan-test andesim-plan-itest andesim-run-test andesim-vsimfilter-test andesim-elf-syms-test andesim-hybrid-test andesim-state-diff-test andesim-engine-registry-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-state-diff-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# hybrid-test reaches plan.hpp via hybrid.hpp; plan.hpp carries the drained
# record (hybrid_state_v1) since verify_oracle F4.
target_include_directories(andesim-hybrid-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andesim driver: driver/ -> build/andesim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andesim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andesim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andesim"

content.text:
Important clarification — thanks. The range **0x0000-0x0527** is the full L2C register block (DS220 Table 112), which mixes register types. That changes the wire-format shape I just drafted (a single `ctrl` word), so let me get the restore policy right before reshaping it, because one part is a genuine hazard.

The range contains:
- **Read-only**: Configuration Register (0x0000) — derived from the build, writes ignored.
- **Boot-static config (writable)**: Control (0x0008), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300-0x0328).
- **Volatile / side-effecting**: CCTL Command registers (0x0040-0x007f) — *writing them re-issues an L2 cache flush/invalidate*; Error registers (0x0030-0x003f) are write-1-clear; CCTL Status / HPM Counters are read-only status.

So draining the whole range is safe and cheap, but writing the whole range back on resume is not.

questions.question: You specified the L2C range 0x0000-0x0527. When vsim resumes at the ROI, how should it write this range back into the hart? (Draining/capturing the full range for the record + --verify is assumed in all options.)

options.label: Restore config regs only (Recommended)
options.description: Capture the full 0x0000-0x0527 range into the handoff record, but on resume write back ONLY the boot-static writable config: Control (0x0008), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Masks (0x0300-0x0328). Never re-issues a CCTL cache command or clears error bits. Correct + cycle-faithful.
options.preview:
drain:   [0x0000 .. 0x0527] raw (record + verify)
restore: 0x0008 Control     (CEN/prefetch/ECC)
         0x0010 HPM Control
         0x0300..0x0328 Way Masks
skip:    0x0000 RO, 0x0040+ CCTL cmd (side-effect),

27	  // scratch_gpa: the GUEST address of the V-register transport page (L26:
28	  // the mmap's top page, v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size)). Defaults to the
29	  // unset sentinel; only the V dump sweep consults it, and it throws there if
30	  // a V drain is reached with the GPA unset (no silent dump to a bogus
31	  // address). The simulator passes the real value from platform.main_memory.
32	  // caps: which Andes custom CSRs the TARGET core implements (from its
33	  // config.inc, supplied by the sim binary). Defaults to all() so existing
34	  // call sites are unchanged. Gates the Andes re-read below: reading an
35	  // unimplemented CSR can stall the DM, same as restoring one.
36	  explicit StateDrain(DmiBus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa = kVScratchGpaUnset,
37	                      AndesCaps caps = AndesCaps::all())
38	      : bus_{bus}, scratch_gpa_{scratch_gpa}, caps_{caps}
39	  {}
40	
41	  // Opt-in PB block-store (dual of ResumeDriver's set_gpr/fpr_block_load):
42	  // drain the GPRs/FPRs with a sd/fsd-sweep into the shared scratch page instead
43	  // of per-register Abstract Command reads. Default OFF; the simulator enables
44	  // both and lifts the swept bytes with read_{gpr,fpr}_from_scratch. Each is
45	  // fits-gated in drain_with_passthrough so a full V page falls back to reads.
46	  void set_gpr_block_store(bool on) { gpr_block_store_ = on; }
47	  void set_fpr_block_store(bool on) { fpr_block_store_ = on; }
48	
49	  // Opt-in Andes+M-ext CSR sweep (dual of ResumeDriver::set_csr_sweep): drain
50	  // the caps-supported CSR block with a Program-Buffer csrr+sd sweep into the CSR
51	  // scratch page instead of one abstract read per CSR. Off by default; the
52	  // simulator enables it and lifts the swept values with read_csr_from_scratch.
53	  void set_csr_sweep(bool on) { csr_sweep_ = on; }
54	
55	  // Drain x1..x31 + PC. FP/CSR/V slots remain zero; merge them in via
56	  // drain_with_passthrough when the QEMU 1 snapshot is available.
57	  auto drain() -> hybrid_state_v1
58	  {
59	    hybrid_state_v1 state{};
60	    state.magic   = HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC;
61	    state.version = HYBRID_STATE_VERSION;
62	    state.flags   = HYBRID_FLAG_RV64;
63	    halt_and_capture_pc_priv(state);
64	
65	    for (uint16_t i = 1; i < 32; ++i)
66	      state.gpr[i] = read_register_64(bus_, regno_gpr(i), "StateDrain GPR");
67	
68	    return state;
69	  }

 *

 *

 *
 * This function does not ensure writes are flushed prior to reading, so
 * callers should take care when calling this function in plugin callbacks to

 * the memory callback API instead.
 *
 * This function is only valid for softmmu targets.
 *

 * address @addr in the current address space for the current vCPU.

// End-to-end roundtrip fixture:
//   1. QEMU + plugin sees `slti x0, x0,  0x5A0` -> drains state, exits.
//   2. vsim resumes, computes a2=3.
//   3. vsim sees `slti x0, x0,  0x5A1` -> drains state, exits 200.
//   4. main spawns qemu-system -gdb -S -semihosting; resume restores GPRs.

    li      a0, 1
    li      a1, 2
    add     a2, a0, a1        // a2 = 3, computed in vsim only

=== semihost_exit.inc ===
// Shared exit-via-semihosting macro for hybrid round-trip fixtures.
//
// SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
//   Builds the {reason=ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit, exit_code=<exit_reg>}
//   16-byte block at 0x00001000, sets a0=SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED (0x20), a1=block,
//   then issues the RISC-V semihosting `slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`
//   triple. exit_reg may be any GPR holding the desired host exit code; this
//   macro clobbers t0, t1, a0, a1.
//
// QEMU's host-exit returns the low 8 bits of <exit_reg> as the process status.

.macro SEMIHOST_EXIT exit_reg
    li      t0, 0x00001000
    li      t1, 0x20026                     // ADP_Stopped_ApplicationExit
    sd      t1, 0(t0)
    sd      \exit_reg, 8(t0)
    li      a0, 0x20                        // SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED
    mv      a1, t0
    .option push
    .option norvc
    slli    x0, x0, 0x1f
    ebreak
    srai    x0, x0, 0x7
    .option pop
99: j       99b
.endm

               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

                  break_verify_diverge

# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's

	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)

	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o

	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# v5 contract: the QEMU plugin drains the L2C MMIO register window into
# hybrid_state_v1. The l2c_drain fixture writes 0xA5 to the L2C Control Register
# (0xE0500008) and then hits the ROI entry marker; the plugin must set
# HYBRID_FLAG_L2C and capture 0xA5 at hybrid_l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL/8].
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     the l2c_drain fixture (FIXTURE=l2c_drain)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-l2c_drain}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

REPO_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-l2c-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
CHECK_SRC=$(mktemp --suffix=.c)
CHECK_BIN=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG" "$CHECK_SRC" "$CHECK_BIN"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Inspect the drained struct via a tiny C checker that shares the ABI header,
# so the field offset stays robust to layout changes.
cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!f) { fprintf(stderr, "open %s failed\n", argv[1]); return 2; }
    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
    size_t n = fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f);
    fclose(f);
    if (n != sizeof(s)) { fprintf(stderr, "short read %zu != %zu\n", n, sizeof(s)); return 3; }
    if (s.magic != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC) { fprintf(stderr, "bad magic\n"); return 4; }
    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
    unsigned long long want = strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 0);
    if (ctrl != want) { fprintf(stderr, "l2c ctrl=0x%llx want=0x%llx\n", ctrl, want); return 6; }
    printf("OK: HYBRID_FLAG_L2C set, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
    return 0;
}
EOF
cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"

if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU" 0xA5; then
  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_drain]"
else
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: L2C register window not drained correctly"
  exit 1
fi

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# v5 contract: QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register (0xE0500008) with its DS220
# 11.8.7 reset value CEN=1 (L2 enabled by default). A fixture that NEVER writes
# the register (handoff_roundtrip) must still drain CEN=1 -- proving a guest that
# relies on the reset default is not silently handed a disabled L2 (CEN=0).
#
# Required environment (auto-detected):
#   VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF (FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

REPO_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-l2c-rst-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
CHECK_SRC=$(mktemp --suffix=.c)
CHECK_BIN=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG" "$CHECK_SRC" "$CHECK_BIN"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi

cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
#include <stdio.h>
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!f) return 2;
    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
    if (fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f) != sizeof(s)) return 3;
    fclose(f);
    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
    if ((ctrl & 0x1u) != 0x1u) { fprintf(stderr, "CEN not set: l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl); return 6; }
    printf("OK: reset default CEN=1, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
    return 0;
}
EOF
cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"

if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU"; then
  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_reset_default]"
else
  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_reset_default]: L2C reset default CEN=1 not observed"
  exit 1
fi

=== CLAUDE.md shared-ABI / v3/v4 block section ===
122:### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
124:`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), and (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
126:**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.
128:Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).

input.old_string: Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).
input.new_string:
**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

+Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).
V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.

It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.

All nine slices are complete and green. Here's the summary.

## What was built

L2 cache controller (L2C) **enable/config transport** across the QEMU→vsim hybrid handoff — the MMIO analog of the existing `mcache_ctl` (L1) transport. The QEMU plugin drains the L2C register window at the handoff; vsim restores the writable config registers via Program-Buffer stores before resuming the ROI; `--verify` re-reads and compares them.

Per your two clarifications, the final scope is: **capture the full `0x0000–0x0527` register window** (DS220 Table 112) into the wire format, but **restore config registers only** — Control (`0x0008`: CEN + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (`0x0010`), Way Allocation Masks (`0x0300–0x0328`). The read-only Configuration register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers, and the W1C error registers are captured but never written back.

## Slices (all TDD: RED → GREEN, tests verified)

| # | Change | Verified |
|---|--------|----------|
| F1 | ABI v5: `struct hybrid_l2c` (1320-byte window) + `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C` + static-asserts | driver+vsim ABI tests |
| F2 | `encode_sw` / `encode_lwu` PB encoders | golden hex from `riscv64-as` |
| F3 | `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` — gated PB `sw`, runs before the GPR loop (scratch safety) | recording-bus unit tests |
| F4 | `StateDrain::drain_l2c` — gated PB `lwu` readback | unit tests + teeth-check |
| F5 | Engine gate: `Simulator::l2c_present()`/`l2c_base()` from `_NDS_L2C_*`, wired to resume+drain | gate logic + header compile |
| F6 | Plugin drains window via `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` + `l2c_base` arg | **real QEMU run** + teeth-check |
| F7 | QEMU seeds L2C Control reset value `CEN=1` at machine init | **real QEMU run** + teeth-check |
| F8 | `state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` (INITSTATUS[14] masked) | driver unit test |
| F9 | Docs (CLAUDE.md, USER_GUIDE.md) + manifest comment | — |

Key safety property: restore is **hard-gated** on the engine having an L2C (a store to an absent region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write). Every current engine is `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the feature no-ops cleanly today and activates when an L2-enabled engine is built.

The end-to-end plugin tests ran against **real QEMU** and confirmed both paths: a guest write of `0xA5` drains through, and a guest that never touches L2C still drains `CEN=1` from the reset seed. The existing plugin test also reported `state size=7504 bytes` — the correct v5 struct size.

## Two things you need to decide on / know

1. **The ABI change is a submodule (`andesim_abi`) edit.** I applied it to both working copies (`andesim/include` and `vsim/external/andesim_abi`) so everything builds and tests locally. To commit properly: commit once in `andesim_abi`, push to your gitea, then bump both submodule pointers.
